angle: Smart home buying as a saving strategy
body_text:
Buying a home can be a saving plan, are you aware?
How do you fully utilise your funds?
✅ Know your loan eligibility
✅ Plan your CPF usage & grants
✅ Think ahead with your exit strategy

Your first home is probably your biggest purchase ever — don’t just buy fast, buy smart.

📩 DM us “PANNA” and get your First-Home Roadmap — let’s plan it right from day one.

headline: Use your home to create a saving plan!
transcript_text: Eh, Jenna, real talk. You know, recently I met a lot of first-time HDB buyers who are ready to buy. But actually, there are so many things they don't know. I agree. Honestly, it's not just about saving up. Because I met so many HDB buyers, they are unaware of their loan eligibility, their CPS usage and their grant. Some of them even have plans to, you know, exit later, but they have no exit plans if they plan to upgrade. And do you realise, the older the flat, the younger the buyers. Exactly. I realise a lot of young buyers choose the older resale flat because of the merchant location, more space and they get to move in immediately. Shorter waiting time as compared to the BTOs. But there are also downsides to it. You're right. Older flats means shorter lease, meaning you can actually limit your CPF usage, your loan options, plus the upkeep cost can be really high because of the renovations, right? On top of that, plus the supply of the new BTOs, older flats may have lower resale value. Makes sense. And the truth is, a lot of first-time buyers don't even come with an agent. They just try to figure it out all themselves. Right, but buying your first home is the biggest purchase of your life. So you want to make sure that you are making the right decision, not a fast one. So if you're a first-time buyer wondering where to start, DM us, Pena, for your first home roadmap. Don't just buy, buy smart!
